specification.outcome: Pi remains visibly responsive while a long-running tiber_workflow_request is evaluating, so the user immediately sees activity and the spinner or progress indicator continues updating until completion.

scenarios.name: show immediate responsive progress
given: a Tiber workflow request starts work that does not complete immediately
then: the user receives an initial progress update before long-running work
Pi's event loop remains available for UI animation and input rendering
bounded progress updates remain visible until the request completes

scenarios.name: avoid progress-update starvation
given: an independent review or repository operation runs for many seconds
then: updates are rate-limited so they do not flood or continually reset Pi's renderer
the final success or typed failure replaces the in-progress state exactly once

scenarios.name: cancel without leaving frozen UI state
given: a long workflow request is active
when: the user cancels it or the request reaches its timeout
then: the underlying work is aborted and timers or subscriptions are disposed
a terminal cancelled or timed-out result is rendered
no progress callback continues after completion

acceptanceCriteria: No synchronous wait or tight progress loop blocks Pi's renderer during workflow requests.
Progress starts promptly, is rate-limited, and has one terminal update.
Cancellation, timeout, success, and failure all clean up progress resources.
The change does not weaken readiness, workflow, role, or effect authorization.
exclusions: Changing workflow policy or review conclusions
Masking genuinely stalled work with fabricated completion
specification.architectureImplications: Keep long work asynchronous and cancellation-aware in the imperative shell. Treat progress as bounded UI observation only; it grants no authority and must be disposed on every terminal path.
